title: How is the angle outside a triangle linked to the inside?
description: A side of the triangle is extended, and the angle outside is found with the angle sum and a straight angle. The same is done for a second triangle, and the outside angle is compared with the inside angles. Keeko's doubt is that it equals the third inside angle.
teaching_notes: One idea: an exterior angle equals the sum of the two inside angles that are not next to it. Watch for students who give the exterior angle the value of the inside angle that sits beside it.

source: The angle formed between the extension of a side of a triangle and the other side is called an exterior angle of the triangle. In this figure, ∠ACD is an exterior angle. Find ∠ACD, if ∠A = 50°, and ∠B = 60°. From the angle sum property, we know that 50° + 60° + ∠ACB = 180°, so ∠ACB = 70°. So, ∠ACD = 180° - 70° = 110°, since ∠ACB and ∠ACD together form a straight angle. Find the exterior angle for different measures of ∠A and ∠B. Do you see any relation between the exterior angle and these two angles?

<bookmark mark='rule'/>Step one, the three angles inside add to one hundred and eighty. Fifty plus sixty plus the angle eigh cee bee is one hundred and eighty.
<bookmark mark='take'/>Take fifty and sixty away from one hundred and eighty, and the angle eigh cee bee is seventy.

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step three, try the second triangle. Thirty five plus forty five plus the angle eigh cee bee is one hundred and eighty.
<bookmark mark='inside'/>That makes the angle eigh cee bee one hundred degrees.
<bookmark mark='take'/>One hundred and eighty take away one hundred is eighty.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Step four, compare each outside angle with the two inside angles not next to it. Fifty plus sixty is one hundred and ten, the outside angle.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Thirty five plus forty five is eighty, the other outside angle.
